name: The Kellogg household at 1923 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_kellogg_mrs_c_p

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1923 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1923 Mrs. C. P. Kellogg; Mrs. Lois Kellogg.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1923, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The one live-in servant it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 is on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. A coachman's wife and children in the rear building are named in his note rather than carded. Left off: Charles Kellogg (written "abroad"; the surname is hard to read). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Mrs. Lois Kellogg
persons.note: Listed at 1923 in both editions. The Blue Book does not say how she was related to Mrs. C. P. Kellogg.

persons.name: Thomas Nelson

born.note: The census gives February 1866, age 33 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Coachman" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as the head of his own household there (coachman); born February 1866, in Sweden, came to the United States in 1884, married. Living with him: Nellie Nelson (wife), Hilda Nelson (daughter), Eugenie Nelson (daughter). Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
